cards.name: Human form run speed and turning
cards.summary: Run speed follows the squared stick value, with fixed per-update acceleration and braking steps and a proportional turn rate.
cards.behavior: The target speed is the run cap times the stick magnitude squared. Half stick therefore gives one quarter of the cap. Speed moves toward the target by the acceleration step times the squared stick value. When speed is above the target, the braking step pulls it down. The acceleration step applies only when the stick value is above 0.3 times the unused share of the speed cap. Stick input counts as present above 0.05. Facing turns toward the stick direction by one fifth of the remaining angle each update. That step is clamped by a maximum and a minimum, and both scale with the squared stick value. If the stick reverses while speed is above 0.6 of the cap, the player does not turn at once. It brakes first, and a turn-around state follows. Room-only areas and several slow states, such as guarding while moving, cap the target at 0.7 of the run cap. The run cap value comes from the move table when the move setup runs.

cards.name: Z-target strafe and backpedal speed
cards.summary: While a target is locked, the player moves with a lower speed cap, much faster acceleration and braking, and a separate backward cap.
cards.behavior: A locked target replaces the run cap with a strafe cap of about 57 percent of the run cap. The acceleration and braking steps are more than three times larger than in free run, so the player starts and stops almost at once. Backward movement has its own cap, acceleration step and braking step. The backward cap is slightly higher than the forward cap when a target is locked. The body turns toward the target every update by half of the remaining angle, up to a large step of 8192. When the lock button is held with no actor locked, a sibling table applies. It has the same forward and strafe cap but a lower backward cap.

cards.name: Steep slope slide and climb limit
cards.summary: Ground steeper than a set angle forces a slide with a high speed cap, and a lower angle sets the climb limit.
cards.behavior: The slide starts when the ground normal tilts past the slide angle. The angle is set in degrees and turned into a cosine threshold when the form is set up. While sliding, speed grows each update by the slide step times a slope factor. The factor runs from 1 on gentle ground to 1.5 on a vertical face. The slide cap is far above the run cap. In water, both the step and the cap shrink to 0.3. A separate climb angle marks the steepest slope that the player can still walk up, and the cap on that slope is lower than the run cap. A landing on a slide polygon skips the land damage check. The wolf form has its own slide table.

cards.name: Forward roll, side hop and backflip
cards.summary: The dodge set uses fixed launch speeds, and the forward roll scales with the speed the player had when it started.
cards.behavior: The forward roll starts at the entry speed times 1.3 plus 3. That value is clamped between a floor of 25 and a ceiling of 3 plus 1.3 times the run cap. Heavy gear and water scale the speed by their own factors. A roll into a wall ends in a crash reaction when the speed is at least 10 and the wall faces the roll. With heavy boots equipped, the roll also arms a hit sphere around the player. The side hop and the back hop use fixed horizontal and vertical launch speeds and then fall under normal gravity. A back input uses the plain backflip when the upper body has no action. Otherwise it uses the back hop.

cards.name: Automatic ledge jump and fall gravity
cards.summary: There is no jump button: leaving a ledge at near full stick launches a fixed-angle forward jump under a constant gravity.
cards.behavior: The jump starts when the player leaves the ground during a move. The stick value must be above 0.85 and the speed must be at least the trigger floor. The player must not wear heavy boots, and the facing must be within a small angle of the move direction. The launch speed is always the jump cap, because the always-max flag is on. That speed is multiplied by 1.3 and split along a fixed launch angle of about 50 degrees. The result is about 26 vertical and 22 horizontal. Gravity is a constant downward step each update, and the fall speed is clamped. Holding backward in the air bleeds off horizontal speed. The effective launch cap is the max jump speed value. The lower limit value only gates the trigger.

cards.name: Ledge height classes
cards.summary: The height of a wall top above the feet picks between walking up, a hop, a pull-up, a jump pull-up and a hang.
cards.behavior: A forward probe finds the wall top and measures its height above the feet. Heights below the walk-up limit are stepped over. The next bands pick a small hop, a normal pull-up, a jump then pull-up, and a jump then hang. The player must push toward the wall for more than 2 updates to start a hop. A grab needs more than 3 updates. While one specific movement mode flag is set, the hang reach is the separate value of 170. The wolf form uses its own set of bands with the same structure.

cards.name: Fall height, landing roll and land damage
cards.summary: The fall height after scaling by one hundredth picks between a soft landing, a roll, small damage and big damage.
cards.behavior: The game stores the height where the fall began. On landing it multiplies the drop by 0.01 and compares the result with fixed bands. A drop between the roll minimum and the roll maximum lets a player who holds the stick forward roll out and take no damage. Below the small band the player lands softly. At or above the small band the player takes small land damage. At or above the big band the damage doubles. Slide polygons skip land damage. A landing from a sword jump strike runs the same bands through a separate check.

cards.name: Sword slash combo and finishers
cards.summary: Plain slashes deal 2 power, finishing strikes deal 3 or 4, and every swing arms a three-capsule blade hit volume.
cards.behavior: Each swing arms three linked capsules along the blade. The capsules share one radius and one length multiplier. Plain slashes use attack power 2. Finishing strikes use power 3, and the two quick-draw sweep finishers use power 4. A finisher that starts from the third combo step uses power 2. Each swing has an attack window given in animation frames and a small forward step speed. The vertical slash is active from frame 5 to 10. The left and right slashes are active from frame 7. The stab finisher is the slowest, with a window from frame 10 to 17. Running swings use a shorter blade multiplier and a smaller radius.

cards.name: Spin attack, jump strike and head-splitting leap
cards.summary: Special sword moves use a growing spin radius, an auto-aimed jump strike and a leap that lands on the target head.
cards.behavior: The spin attack starts with a hit sphere of radius 130. The sphere grows each update toward a final radius during the attack window. The enlarged spin state grows faster, reaches a larger radius and hits harder at power 4. The plain spin has power 3. Holding the sword button for about three updates marks a spin charge. The jump strike launches at a base speed pair. With a locked target, the code solves the horizontal speed from the flight time and caps the horizontal distance at 500. The head-splitting leap has its own gravity. It clamps the target height and distance, then solves the speeds that end above the target head. The large jump strike adds a landing blast with its own radius.

cards.name: Shield guard knockback
cards.summary: A blocked hit pushes the player back at a speed set by the attack size class.
cards.behavior: When the shield stops a hit, the player slips backward. The slip speed depends on the size class of the attack. Normal hits push at 14, large hits push at 20, and huge hits push at 26. A magnetic-pull attack has two more values, and heavy gear uses the lower one. Two special arenas replace the huge push with 40 when the player is not wearing heavy gear.

cards.name: Horse speed, braking and turning
cards.summary: The horse has a high speed cap, gentle acceleration and a turn limit, and its target speed follows the stick.
cards.behavior: The target speed is the cap times the squared stick value times the cosine of the stick angle relative to the horse heading. It is floored at zero. Speed chases that target with a small acceleration step. It falls with a smaller braking step when the stick is released. A larger stopping step applies for walls and events. Turning uses a divisor of five between a minimum and a maximum step. When the stick points backward, the horse brakes and then walks backward at a low cap. A walk floor stops the horse from creeping below a minimum speed while the stick is held. Five designated field areas use a table with a lower cap.

cards.name: Horse spur dash and spur recovery
cards.summary: Each spur adds a timed speed boost, and spur charges refill on timers.
cards.behavior: The rider can store up to six spurs. A spur sets a boost timer. While the timer runs, the speed cap rises by the spur bonus and the horse accelerates at the spur step. The horse never drops below a minimum speed while boosted. Spending the last spur starts a long timer that refills all six at once. Spending any other spur starts a shorter timer that adds one spur. Later refills then come at a fast interval until the count is full. The lower-cap field table also has a smaller spur bonus.

cards.name: Horse ballistic jump
cards.summary: The horse jumps by solving gravity and flight time for a target distance, so the arc always reaches the landing point.
cards.behavior: A jump starts at a cliff edge or when a downed boar-type enemy lies ahead. The code sets a target horizontal distance and height. Forward speed is raised to at least three quarters of the speed cap. The flight time is the distance over the speed, with a minimum of three updates. A first gravity value is solved so the rise reaches the target height after that time. A second value, solved the same way, drives the descent. Landing keeps eighty percent of the jump speed and resets gravity to the default. The downed-enemy jump clears a distance of 350 and a height of 150. A cliff jump uses a horizontal distance of 125.

cards.name: Mounted sword combat
cards.summary: On horseback the rider swings short quick slashes with a longer blade and a larger radius, plus a charged spin.
cards.behavior: Mounted slashes use a longer blade multiplier and a wider radius than slashes on foot. Attack power stays at 2. In a one-on-one mounted duel the blade grows again. Each side slash is active for four frames starting at frame 2. A six-frame morph then returns the rider to the riding pose. The charged mounted spin has a very large radius and an active window of 25 frames. The rider can also use the bow, the boomerang and the clawshot while riding. The boomerang adds the horse forward speed to its own.

cards.name: Wolf run speed and timed dash
cards.summary: The wolf has a base run cap, a timed dash mode with a higher cap, and a cooldown before the next dash.
cards.behavior: Outside dash mode the wolf run cap is 25, with an acceleration step of 3 and a braking step of 1.8. The dash action starts dash mode. The launch speed is raised to at least 65. Speed then chases a cap of 45 with an acceleration step of 6 and a braking step of 3. Dash mode lasts 90 updates and then clears. A cooldown of 50 updates starts when the dash animation ends. Slippery or snowy ground uses slower dash profiles with lower launch speed, cap and duration. Locking on or gazing with no actor lowers the cap to 22. The table also lists a plain cap of 40 for dash mode. The branch that would use it tests the same flag as the branch above it, so it never runs. Treat 45 as the live dash cap.

cards.name: Wolf locked strafe, hops and auto jump
cards.summary: The wolf strafes faster when locked on, hops farther, and its auto jump has a dash profile and a weaker profile.
cards.behavior: The wolf locked strafe cap is 18 with an acceleration step of 2, and the rear cap is 12. The side hop and the back hop use fixed launch speeds that exceed the human values. The wolf auto jump has two profiles. In dash mode it launches at an angle of about 41 degrees. The entry speed is set to the cap of 38 and multiplied by 1.1. That gives about 28 vertical and 31 horizontal. Outside dash mode a weaker profile launches at about 45 degrees with a cap of 31 and a multiplier of 1.02. Gravity is a constant 3.6 downward each update and the fall cap is 100.

cards.name: Wolf lock-on leap and jump bite
cards.summary: The wolf lock-on leap flies to the target at a fixed speed, and the jump attack has a standard and a dash profile.
cards.behavior: The lock-on leap aims at the eye position of the locked target. The vertical offset clamps between 10 and 700, and the horizontal distance clamps at 1000. The flight time is the distance divided by the leap speed of 85, never below one update. Gravity is solved so the arc ends at the target, and a gravity of -8 applies after the flight time ends. The hit cylinder deals attack power 6, with radius 60 and height 120. The jump attack has two profiles. The standard profile launches at 30 with caps of 40 horizontal and 23 vertical, and deals power 2, or power 3 on the fourth combo step. The dash profile has caps of 45 and 35 and deals power 3. With a locked target, both profiles aim at the target eye height. Some table values for lock circle growth are not read by any code, so they are not live behavior.

cards.name: Clawshot fire, return and pull speed
cards.summary: The clawshot head flies at a fixed speed, returns faster, and pulls the player along the chain at a set step.
cards.behavior: The hook head flies out at the shoot speed until it reaches the maximum length or hits something. On a miss it returns at the return speed. When it carries a caught item or enemy back, the return speed drops to the lower stick-return value. After the head hooks a pull point, the player moves toward the head each update. The step is the stick-return value plus the distance the head moved in that update. The pull ends when the remaining distance is below that step. A large boss arena swaps in a table with longer chain and higher speeds. A roof hook lets the player rise and descend by stick, and both steps scale with stick magnitude.

cards.name: Boomerang, bow and slingshot flight data
cards.summary: Thrown and shot items read speed and range from fixed tables, with charge and scope variants and a rider speed bonus.
cards.behavior: The boomerang flies at a fixed speed with a longer range on horseback, and it adds the horse forward speed. Its lock range is the larger of the lock table value and the fly range. An arrow picks its data in a fixed order. The slingshot comes first. A scope view comes next, then a charged shot, then the plain shot. Bomb arrows have their own slower rows. A charged arrow is the fastest. The scope arrow is next, and it has the same long range. A plain arrow is slower. A charged shot needs the charge hold timer to run out.

cards.name: Swim speed, buoyancy and fall limits
cards.summary: Swim speed caps depend on direction and gear, and water gravity is a small constant that heavy boots raise.
cards.behavior: Surface swim has a forward cap of 8, a strafe cap of 8 and a backward cap of 6. A swim dash has a cap of 13. Heavy boots use an underwater walk cap of 8. The acceleration step is 5 times the stick value, and the braking step is 0.5. In water the gravity is the buoyancy value, so the body sinks slowly. Heavy boots use a stronger gravity of -0.7 and a fall cap of -20. Without heavy gear the fall cap in water is -4. Swimming starts once the water is deeper than the start height. The wolf form uses a faster table with a cap of 20 and stronger sinking.

cards.name: Z-target candidate weighting and release
cards.summary: Lock-on candidates are ranked by distance with an angle penalty, held in short lists, and released at a larger distance than they were gained.
cards.behavior: Each candidate gets a weight equal to its distance times a factor between 0.5 and 1. The factor grows with the square of the angle off the player facing. The lowest weight wins. The game keeps up to eight lock-on candidates and four candidates each for action prompts and check objects. A candidate must lie inside a table entry for its type. The entry holds a maximum distance, a larger release distance, an angle-based extra reach and vertical limits. A target stays locked until it falls outside the release distance, so the lock has a hysteresis band. Hold mode is the default lock setting.

cards.name: Lock-on camera defaults and limits
cards.summary: The lock-on camera blends on a set timer, limits its pitch to a fixed range and drops a forced lock at a distance or time limit.
cards.behavior: The camera setup holds default blend and limit values. A lock target change blends over 40 updates with a blend share of 0.25 per update. Special cases replace the 40 with 5, 40 or 60. The camera pitch is clamped between -60 and 80 degrees. A forced lock ends when the target is farther than 3500 units, when the lock lasts longer than 90 updates, or when the player locks on by hand. When the camera orbit radius falls below 70 units, or 120 for the wolf, the camera flags the player model for hiding. The near and far clip planes are 1 and 100000. These are constructor defaults, and per-area camera styles can override many of them.

cards.name: Hit invincibility and knockback
cards.summary: A hit grants a fixed invincibility time, and knockback speed depends on the hit class.
cards.behavior: After a hit the player is invincible for 30 updates. A normal hit starts the knockback at 10 plus 0.02 times the horizontal hit vector length. The braking step is 1 per update. A large hit launches at 20 horizontal and 30 vertical under a gravity of -5. It then bounces at 15. The wolf form has its own matching tables.
